Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Exercises ./ledger against a fresh database and compares every command's exit code and standard\n# output with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/LayersTesting/bin/run.sh APP  from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Database: DATABASE_URL when the caller sets it (for example a PostgreSQL DSN), otherwise a\n# SQLite file in a fresh temporary directory. Every run starts with `ledger init`, so the grader\n# never depends on prior state. Exit 0 only when every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/seed_accounts.csv\" ]; then SEED=$HERE; else SEED=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nLEDGER=\"$APP/ledger\"\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nDATABASE_URL=${DATABASE_URL:-$WORK/ledger.db}\nexport DATABASE_URL\n\nif [ ! -x \"$LEDGER\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: no executable ./ledger at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is an executable named ledger at the application root.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <ledger args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$LEDGER\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: ledger $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: ledger $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. Schema lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck A1 0 init < /dev/null\ncheck A2 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,0\ncategories,0\ntransactions,0\nEOF\n\n# ── B. Bulk load of the known dataset ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck B1 0 load accounts \"$SEED/seed_accounts.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\naccounts,4\nEOF\ncheck B2 0 load categories \"$SEED/seed_categories.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ncategories,7\nEOF\ncheck B3 0 load transactions \"$SEED/seed_transactions.csv\" <<'EOF'\ntable,loaded\ntransactions,120\nEOF\ncheck B4 0 count <<'EOF'\ntable,rows\naccounts,4\ncategories,7\ntransactions,120\nEOF\n?? Command modules call ``register`` on import; nothing else edits it.\"\"\"\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli.errors import UsageError\n\nHandler = Callable[[list[str]], list[list[str]] | None]\n\n_COMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], tuple[Handler, tuple[int, int]]] = {}\n\n\ndef register(words: tuple[str, ...], handler: Handler, nargs: tuple[int, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Add a command. ``words`` is its name, ``nargs`` is the (min, max) argument count after it.\"\"\"\n    if not words:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command needs at least one word\")\n    if words in _COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command already registered: {' '.join(words)}\")\n    low, high = nargs\n    if low < 0 or high < low:\n        raise ValueError(f\"invalid argument count {nargs!r} for {' '.join(words)}\")\n    _COMMANDS[tuple(words)] = (handler, (low, high))\n\n\ndef lookup(argv: list[str]) -> tuple[Handler, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return the handler for the longest registered word prefix of ``argv`` and its arguments.\"\"\"\n    for size in range(len(argv), 0, -1):\n        entry = _COMMANDS.get(tuple(argv[:size]))\n        if entry is not None:\n            handler, (low, high) = entry\n            args = argv[size:]\n            if not low <= len(args) <= high:\n                raise UsageError(f\"{' '.join(argv[:size])}: expects {_count(low, high)} argument(s)\")\n            return handler, args\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given\")\n    raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {' '.join(argv)}\")\n\n\ndef _count(low: int, high: int) -> str:\n    return str(low) if low == high else f\"{low} to {high}\"\n"}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPGp35jxHygBjAU8WRaS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019ob14Xh1EutV6vzUGc77ja","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261025.160726/build/LayersTesting/cli/context.py","content":"\"\"\"Opens the declared store for a command. The only caller of ``persistence.open_database``.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nfrom cli.config import resolve_dsn\n\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by the environment, creating a missing SQLite parent directory first.\"\"\"\n    dsn = resolve_dsn(os.environ)\n    path = _sqlite_path(dsn)\n    if path is not None:\n        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return open_database(dsn)\n\n\ndef _sqlite_path(dsn: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the file path a SQLite DSN names, or None for any other engine.\"\"\"\n    if dsn.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        return dsn[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn\n    return None\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6490,"cache_read_input_tokens":61460,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6490},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6410a10e-6874-454d-bef2-272c00dfcb3f","uuid":"b1e1dffb-1c4f-4558-abd1-6a17303d4328","timestamp":"2026-10-25T16:30:26.892Z","request_id":"req_011CgPGp2qMrW58vSeHTfQLd","wire_tool_inputs":{"toolu_019ob14Xh1EutV6vzUGc77ja":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/LayersTesting/runs/20261025.160726/build/LayersTesting/cli/context.py","content":"\"\"\"Opens the declared store for a command. The only caller of ``persistence.open_database``.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nfrom cli.config import resolve_dsn\n\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by the environment, creating a missing SQLite parent directory first.\"\"\"\n    dsn = resolve_dsn(os.environ)\n    path = _sqlite_path(dsn)\n    if path is not None:\n        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    return open_database(dsn)\n\n\ndef _sqlite_path(dsn: str) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the file path a SQLite DSN names, or None for any other engine.\"\"\"\n    if dsn.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        return dsn[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if \"://\" not in dsn:\n        return dsn\n    return None\n"}}}

Both are done, with one caveat on the database story.\n\n- **database:** The declaration is `blueprint/DATABASE.md`, which is protected and already contains the three tables and every operation. I wrote no persistence code. The generated `persistence/` package and `schema.sql` are already in the build and match the declaration (the `clear` operations are present). Nothing needed writing here.\n- **cli-entry:** I built the `cli` package to FEATURE-CliEntry.md:\n  - `main(argv) -> int` finds the longest registered word prefix, checks the argument count, runs the handler, then writes its rows as unquoted CSV with LF endings.\n  - A `LedgerError` returns its code, and a `PersistenceError` or any other exception returns 1. Each writes one diagnostic line to stderr and nothing to stdout.\n  - `main` imports every module in `cli.commands` before dispatching, so later commands register without editing `main`.\n  - `resolve_dsn` and `open_store` follow the spec. `open_store` creates the SQLite parent directory and does not apply schema.\n\nChoices I made, for you to redirect:\n- `register` raises `ValueError` on a duplicate command name, an empty word tuple, or an inverted argument range.\n- I did not create `cli/core.py`. It needs `init`, `load`, `count` and the rest of the commands, which later blocks add, so it is not expected to pass yet.
